# NIPAT 0.6.0 evidence for pre-1.0 publication

## Decision

Maintainer Gregorio Dalia authorized 0.6 as a pre-1.0 development reference on the strength of automated checks and non-exhaustive installation and operation tests on his PC. The intended release for domain researchers was 0.7. This decision did not establish completion of the entire desktop acceptance matrix or general scientific validity.

## Reported Windows observations

Gregorio Dalia reported the results on 25 October 2026 for Windows 11 x64 with WSL2 already available. This account transcribes the maintainer's logs. It does not describe a newly executed automated test or direct access to his PC.

The installed application's manifest identified version `0.6.0`, source `f062b2376b1fe115c1b68dc50ad697efee1b40d0` and `phase: ready`, without `last_error`. Diagnostics identified the runtime and verified the contracts for DNPcall, SNPcall, Contamination and CPI. Tests completed the following checks:

- SNPcall produced nine rows matching the distributed reference.
- CPI produced the expected values for an informative pair and a no-site case, with three PDFs.
- Contamination produced expected per-site and summary results with and without `ratio_REF_ALT`, and for a no-site case.
- Four external-input checks, including multi-panel and ALL CPI, preserved the original files.

A subsequent BAM-based DNPcall analysis returned `status: succeeded` with eleven sites. Counts and genotypes agreed with the maintainer's reported operational reference. Genetic data, sample names and personal paths were excluded from this public record. The SHA-256 of the installed EXE was unavailable. These findings belong to the source identified by its manifest, not to the bytes of the two installers below.

## Candidate packages

[Manual build 40218369232](https://github.com/GregorioDalia/nipat-desktop/actions/runs/40218369232) passed all required checks on `eb1601885da0d0038ea2f928055e0656368fa58d`, an ancestor of main. [Main CI](https://github.com/GregorioDalia/nipat-desktop/actions/runs/40218609531) passed at `42199c7f4d9e3b7cdff7550ba6ee2abacb02eb49`.

| `NIPAT-Setup.exe` | `2901cb07ca3c49eca72fa7beb7e663c4f257dea0c61cf07e78dc6b1643bec046` |
| `nipat-desktop_0.6.0_amd64.deb` | `ad48f1b99c303cb45835b039e23f29c0a0e88a8129b6a644544b75e742c07604` |

Checks included Python and Windows tests, R regressions inside the image, loading the exported runtime, compiling the EXE and verifying the package pair. The Ubuntu runner installed the DEB and ran four analyses as a non-root user, verified unchanged inputs, reinstalled and removed the package, and preserved user data and unrelated Docker resources. A separate Ubuntu container initially lacked the dependencies and verified that APT installed them.

## Limited reuse of previous evidence

Before preparation or publication, the publisher compared the operational files distributed from the observed commit and the candidate: application, R scripts, scientific setup, configuration, installers, builders and runtime definitions in the inventory. Documentation and CI/publication tooling were excluded. The only permitted removal was the pair of old signature-verification helpers. Any other difference in those files stopped this route.

The results were recorded in `baseline-source-check.json`. Matching sources did not establish binary identity or repeat the physical desktop trial on the new installers. The maintainer explicitly accepted this limitation for 0.6.

## Deferred checks

The outstanding Windows scenarios were a clean system with WSL activation, controlled coexistence with previous installations and the complete reinstall/removal matrix. Outstanding interactive Ubuntu Desktop cases included a clean installation, pre-existing Docker and reinstall/removal. Runner checks retain their actual scope.

Researchers planned to evaluate representative inputs and interpret results on 0.7. Planned automated coverage included parameter boundaries, chained analyses and error handling. Unperformed checks remained identified in the publication record.
